transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t get rid of this feeling that I’m being punished for letting my father decline. My sister shows me the doctor’s notes and tells me I did everything I could, but... it doesn’t change it. It feels like judgment has already been passed on me.
Can you tell me when your father's health decline or passing occurred, and how long ago you first started feeling this way?
It started about a year and two months ago, when my father’s health and behavior began changing and I had to take on caregiving. The feeling has been there since then.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you used to enjoy for most of the day, nearly every day?
Yes. Most days I wake up feeling heavy and hollow, like the color has gone out of everything. I’ll be at my desk in HR or looking at my garden, and it just… none of it reaches me anymore.

When your sister shows you the doctor's notes proving you did everything you could, do you find yourself still absolutely certain, beyond any doubt, that you are being punished and judged—as if it's an unshakeable fact—or do you recognize intellectually that this feeling might not be true?
I know what she’s showing me, but it doesn’t change it. I’m still certain I’m being punished. It feels like the judgment was already made, and there’s nothing the notes can say that changes that.

Before this past year, have you ever gone through a separate period—at any earlier point in your life—where you felt persistently down, lost interest in things, and had similar symptoms for two weeks or more, followed by a time when you felt back to your normal self?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time before this that was like what you’re describing.

Have you ever, at any point before your father's illness, experienced a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt unusually sad, low, or uninterested in things, even if it wasn't as severe as what you're feeling now?
I don’t really remember having a stretch like this before. Lately, though, most days I wake up feeling heavy and hollow, and even things like my work or the garden just don’t seem to reach me.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a single episode (no prior history of depressive or manic episodes) of depressed mood, anhedonia, and psychomotor/cognitive heaviness present most of the day, nearly every day, for over a year, precipitated by caregiving strain and loss related to her father's decline. Critically, she holds a fixed, mood-congruent delusion of guilt ('I am being punished,' 'judgment has already been passed') that persists despite clear contradictory evidence (sister's reassurance and documentation), indicating a delusional (psychotic) belief rather than mere rumination or exaggerated guilt. The combination of a severe depressive syndrome with a congruent psychotic feature meets criteria for Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, Severe with Psychotic Features (F32.3). Adjustment disorder is excluded given the psychotic symptom and severity/duration exceeding typical adjustment reactions, and recurrent depressive disorder is excluded as no prior discrete episode was identified.
